chunks: By this chain of narration, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Muhammad ibn Sa'id, from Atiyya al-Awfi, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, from the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), who said:

Whoever says 'Bismillah (In the name of God)' when he leaves his house, the two angels say: 'You have been guided.' If he then says 'La hawla wala quwwata illa billah (There is no ability nor power except by God),' they say: 'You have been safeguarded.' If he then says 'Tawakkaltu alallah (I rely on God),' they say: 'You have been sufficed.' Then Satan says: 'How can I deal with a servant who has been guided, safeguarded, and sufficed?!'

key_terms.بسم الله: Bismillah — 'In the name of God'; an invocation of divine blessing at the start of any action
key_terms.توكلت على الله: Tawakkaltu alallah — 'I rely upon God'; expresses trust and submission to divine will
key_terms.كفيت: Kufita — 'You have been sufficed'; God takes care of all the person's needs
key_terms.لا حول ولا قوة إلا بالله: La hawla wala quwwata illa billah — 'There is no ability or power except by God'; expresses complete dependence on God
key_terms.هديت: Hudita — 'You have been guided'; passive form indicating divine act
key_terms.وقيت: Wuqita — 'You have been safeguarded/protected'; divine protection

ai.seo_question: What supplication should a Muslim recite when leaving the house?
ai.summary: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) describes a three-part supplication for leaving the house: bismillah invokes divine guidance, la hawla wala quwwata illa billah seeks protection, and tawakkaltu alallah ensures full sufficiency. When all three are recited, Satan himself acknowledges his inability to harm such a person. This hadith, transmitted through Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, belongs to a well-known tradition in both Sunni and Shia sources encouraging dhikr upon leaving the home.

en.bilal-muhammad: By this isnad from Muhammad b. Abi `Umayr from Aban b. `Uthman from Muhammad b. Sa`id from `Atiyya al-`Awfi from Abi Sa`id al-Khudri from the Prophet (s).

He said: Whoever says: “in the name of Allah (bismillah)” when he leaves his house, the two angels say: “You have been guided.” When he says: “there is no ability nor power except by Allah (la hawla wala quwwata illa billah)”, they say: “You have been safeguarded.” When he says: “I rely on Allah (tawakkaltu `alallah)”, they say: “You have been sufficed.” Then, Satan will say: “How could I handle a worshiper who is guided, safeguarded, and sufficed?!”
